brief: Goldman equity sales note arguing energy is the transmission channel into rates and equities. The US struck Iranian air defense, radar and communications around Hormuz while oil was already rising during market hours, Iran retaliated against military rather than energy assets, and crude, distillates and European natural gas all pushed higher. Rising commodity inflation is no longer only a term premium story: it is pulling the front end as the market prices a greater chance the Fed responds, so a supply shock hits growth at the same time policy is pushed toward tightening, which pressures multiples. Europe is the most exposed leg because gas is higher and Russia-linked sub-NATO-threshold attacks are spreading into infrastructure and aviation, which the author calls a meaningful tail risk. The offset is hardware, where Dell beat with AI server and CPU demand accelerating, Palo Alto Networks raised guidance, and Broadcom reports tonight. Conclusion: if crude, gas and product prices fall, yields can stabilize and risk can recover provided NFP and CPI cooperate. If energy keeps rising, sustained upside becomes much harder.
